symptom: While customers browse public VII pages, a full-page 'the page did not load fully' boundary can replace the requested page. On dated vacation-complex pages, only the supplier-selected cheapest unit receives a verified price while sibling suites show incomplete availability information.
expected_behavior: Ordinary navigation must render only the requested page without starting unrelated maintenance. A dated whole-complex visit must keep every published unit visible and independently verify availability, restrictions, price and booking identity for every unit that can fit the selected party.
environment: Reported on public vii.spaplus.co Sites version 661 on 2026-10-25 during repeated desktop and mobile navigation and on a dated multi-unit vacation detail page. Local repair candidate is branch release/v646-four-gaps after version 661 source commit 03688236c4289ccb57291b2c2e71a6c873a4cf50.

steps: Navigate repeatedly among public home, search and business pages and observe the global error boundary reported by the user.
Open a multi-unit vacation property with from, till and guests parameters.
Inspect the suites and units section after the supplier responses settle.
reproduction.evidence: The supplied screenshots show the global error boundary during search navigation and one priced unit beside sibling units without a supplier-confirmed result. Source tracing showed every anonymous HTML request starting catalog synchronization and the complete quality runner, while the detail page consumed supplierStayQuote.roomIDs from only the cheapest search selection.

observations.observation: Every anonymous HTML fetch that passed shouldStartQualityHeartbeat started both runSupplierCatalogScheduleTick and runQualityChecks through waitUntil.
observations.evidence: worker/index.ts before the repair; the same maintenance already has a dedicated scheduled handler.

observations.observation: The previous room-card logic assigned the whole-property supplier quote only when its cheapest room ID matched a card and used the calendar only for broad availability of other rooms.
observations.evidence: app/business/client-page.tsx before the repair and the user-provided multi-unit screenshot.

observations.observation: The exact supplier vacancy endpoint accepts a specific roomID and validates that same room, dates, party, total and booking capability.

hypotheses.mechanism: Visitor navigation incorrectly owns catalog synchronization and full QQQAAA execution, so ordinary page loads can exhaust the Cloudflare Worker resource budget and surface the global error boundary.
hypotheses.prediction: The public fetch path contains both expensive pipelines even though scheduled() already owns them; removing them from fetch leaves scheduled maintenance intact and the build/navigation contracts valid.
hypotheses.discriminating_test: Inspect the fetch and scheduled handlers separately, remove only visitor-triggered maintenance, and run the navigation regression plus the production build.
hypotheses.result: Before repair fetch contained both pipelines. After repair fetch contains neither, scheduled() retains both owners, the focused regression passes and the production build completes.

hypotheses.mechanism: All reported global boundaries are only stale browser assets during a deployment.
hypotheses.prediction: The failure should be limited to known chunk or RSC asset mismatch messages and source inspection should reveal no request-budget pressure on ordinary navigation.
hypotheses.discriminating_test: Compare the observed generic recurring failure with the worker request path and classify known deployment asset errors separately.
hypotheses.result: Known chunk/RSC mismatch is a possible secondary deployment-time case, but it does not explain the expensive maintenance attached to every HTML request. A one-shot cache recovery was added only for recognized asset errors, while generic errors remain visible and do not reload-loop.

hypotheses.mechanism: The supplier exposes only one suite result for a whole complex.
hypotheses.prediction: The accepted detail snapshot would contain only the selected room and the exact vacancy API would reject other room IDs.
hypotheses.discriminating_test: Compare accepted roomOptions with the quote path and exercise supplierStayQuote using explicit room IDs.
hypotheses.result: Accepted detail contains the sibling units and supplierStayQuote supports exact room IDs. The loss occurred in the frontend aggregation, which consumed only the cheapest search result.

fix.change: Make scheduled() the sole owner of catalog and quality maintenance; add a bounded one-time recovery only for recognized release-asset mismatches; add a bounded-concurrency room-scoped quote endpoint and consume each exact room quote in its matching card and booking link.
fix.evidence: The production build passes, 50 focused affected-family tests pass, and the new QQQAAA suite asserts visitor isolation, bounded release recovery, complete room fan-out, failure isolation and exact booking room IDs.

affected_family: public home, search and business navigation
scheduled catalog refresh and QQQAAA ownership
room-specific prices, restrictions and booking links
last-minute deep links that identify one source room

regression_checks.check: Production build includes the new API route and compiles all client and Worker changes.
Visitor fetch no longer starts maintenance while scheduled maintenance remains present.
Every requested room produces an ordered result and one supplier failure remains isolated to that room.
Existing quote validation, booking, PWA, cache and quality-platform contracts remain intact.

remaining_unknowns: Exact post-release production navigation and supplier responses must still be verified against the deployed version before completion is claimed.
authorization_boundary: Repair, test, publish and verify the public VII code and QQQAAA coverage. No real booking, destructive data action, DNS change or unrelated product change.
